sourceTitleEnglish: Contrast a habit and an event
sourceObjectiveEnglish: Contrast a habit and an event: Use the imperfect for past habits or background: estudiaba, comía, vivía.
sourceFocusEnglish: Contrast a habit and an event
sourceSpeakingEnglish: Role-play Antes y ayer with a patient classmate. Practice contrast a habit and an event. Use this lesson's grammar, ask a related question, answer the partner, and confirm understanding. Keep language at beginner level; explain unfamiliar words in English when asked.

sourceGrammarEnglish.focus: Use the imperfect for past habits or background: estudiaba, comía, vivía. It presents an ongoing or repeated past situation rather than its completed boundary.

examples.en: I used to live near Julia.
We used to study together on Mondays.

cards.decisionNote: French sac à dos is masculine while source mochila is feminine; map dictionary and saved item context.
Spanish la groups feminine article, it and her; French la/l’ needs a noun or object role and can elide.
French une aligns only with a feminine noun; source una is feminine.
The backpack changes grammatical gender: source una mochila, French un sac à dos.
Source en groups in/on/at; French dans, sur, à or au depends on context.
French bleu agrees with masculine sac à dos, whereas source mochila azul is feminine.
Spanish los is masculine plural article/object; French les is gender-neutral and role-dependent.
Source de is of/from; French de, du and de la depend on following phrase.
Source cerca covers near/nearby; French près de versus tout près depends on construction.

cards.sourceEnglish: I used to live near Julia.
cards.decisionNote: Spanish imperfect vivía and French imparfait habitais align conditionally; Master-stage progression still needs curriculum review.

cards.sourceEnglish: We used to study together on Mondays.
cards.decisionNote: Spanish plural los lunes signals habitual Mondays; French le lundi is habitual singular construction.

cards.sourceEnglish: Yesterday I went to her house.
cards.decisionNote: The source says went to her house; French suis allé(e) requires speaker gender, while chez elle can hide the physical house sense. No single face is selected.

cards.sourceEnglish: We spoke Spanish for an hour.
cards.proposedFrench: Nous avons parlé espagnol pendant une heure.
cards.decisionNote: Spanish hablamos can be present or preterite by form; source English pins past spoke. French passé composé is conditional.

cards.proposedFrench: La visite a été très agréable.
cards.decisionNote: Spanish fue treats the visit as completed event; French a été versus était changes event/background framing.

cards.sourceSpanish: Antes vivía cerca de la escuela.
cards.sourceEnglish: I used to live near the school.
I used to study Spanish in the afternoon.
cards.decisionNote: Source por la tarde is in the afternoon as a past habit; French l’après-midi is contextual.

reader.sourceSpanish: Antes vivía cerca de la escuela.
reader.sourceEnglish: I used to live near the school.
I used to study Spanish in the afternoon.
reader.decisionNote: Source Spanish-study scene remains; French proposal teaches study of Spanish only as source evidence.

reader.sourceEnglish: Ana used to walk to the library.
reader.proposedFrench: Ana allait à pied à la bibliothèque.
reader.decisionNote: Ana used to walk to the library; allait à pied is habitual movement rather than a single completed trip.

reader.sourceEnglish: We used to eat together on Fridays.
reader.decisionNote: Spanish los viernes is recurring Fridays; French le vendredi is habitual usage.

reader.proposedFrench: Luis avait un sac à dos bleu.
reader.decisionNote: Backpack is masculine in French and adjective bleu agrees with sac à dos.

reader.sourceEnglish: Now we live in another city.
reader.proposedFrench: Maintenant, nous habitons dans une autre ville.
reader.decisionNote: Now marks present contrast; French maintenant/nous habitons retains another city.

sourceDecisions: The source objective teaches Spanish imperfect for past habits/background and contrasts a completed yesterday event; French imparfait versus passé composé is conditional and needs qualified curriculum review at Master stage.
Source una mochila is feminine but French un sac à dos is masculine. Keep noun, article and adjective agreement explicit in selected teaching, dictionary and saved items.
Source la, los, en, de and cerca group context-sensitive article, object and preposition senses; do not score one context-free French face.
Ayer fui a su casa leaves narrator gender unspecified and describes her house. Choose a natural French form without silently assigning gender or dropping the house meaning.
The past-event value of hablamos and fue, recurring Mondays/Fridays, Spanish-study scene and now-city contrast need exact source and register review.
